overview: Luxembourg is a small landlocked country between Belgium, France and Germany. Its capital, Luxembourg City, is one of the official seats of the European Union. It is the only grand duchy left in the world, and its official languages are Luxembourgish, French and German. Luxembourg has one of the highest incomes per person in the world, thanks largely to banking and finance.

geography.text: The north of Luxembourg, called the Ösling, is part of the forested Ardennes uplands. The south, called the Gutland or 'good land', is lower and more fertile, and is where most people live. The Moselle river forms part of the border with Germany, and its valley is lined with vineyards.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Mild and damp, with cool summers and cold winters in the hilly north.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: Wild boar and deer live in the Ardennes forests in the north.

history.text: Luxembourg began as a castle built in 963. Over the centuries it was ruled by Burgundy, Spain, Austria and France. It became a grand duchy in 1815 and was declared permanently neutral in 1867. Occupied by Germany in both World Wars, it then became a founding member of NATO and of what is now the European Union.

events.title: Castle founded
events.text: Count Siegfried acquires the rock on which Luxembourg City grows.

events.title: Grand duchy
events.text: The Congress of Vienna makes Luxembourg a grand duchy.

events.title: Neutrality
events.text: The Treaty of London declares Luxembourg permanently neutral.

events.title: German occupation
events.text: Germany occupies Luxembourg during the Second World War.

events.title: Founding member of the EEC
events.text: Luxembourg helps found what becomes the European Union.

government.text: Luxembourg is the world's only grand duchy. The Grand Duke is head of state, and the Prime Minister leads the government. Its parliament, the Chamber of Deputies, has 60 members. Luxembourg was a founding member of NATO and of what is now the European Union, and several EU institutions are based there.

economy.text: Luxembourg has the highest income per person in the world. Banking and investment funds are the biggest industry, and many international companies have offices there. Steel was once the main industry; ArcelorMittal, one of the world's largest steelmakers, is still based in the capital. Public transport is free for everyone.

culture.text: Luxembourgers commonly speak three languages: Luxembourgish, French and German, and most also speak English. The capital is built on cliffs above two rivers, with old fortifications listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Three languages
items.text: Luxembourgish, French and German are all used in everyday life.

items.title: The Bock Casemates
items.text: Tunnels carved into the rock beneath the old fortress.

items.title: Free public transport
items.text: Since 2020, the first country to make all public transport free.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Judd mat Gaardebounen, smoked pork with broad beans, is the national dish.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: The capital's old quarters and fortifications are a UNESCO site, and the country hosts many music festivals.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: The Dancing Procession of Echternach, listed by UNESCO, sees thousands hop through the streets every Whit Tuesday.

sport.text: Cycling is Luxembourg's most successful sport: its riders have won the Tour de France five times, including Andy Schleck in 2010. Football is the most popular sport to play.

items.title: Tour de France
items.text: Five wins, from François Faber in 1909 to Andy Schleck in 2010.

items.title: Josy Barthel
items.text: Won the 1,500 m at the 1952 Olympics, Luxembourg's only Olympic gold.

didYouKnow: Luxembourg was the first country to make all public transport free, in 2020.
Luxembourg is the world's only remaining grand duchy.

keyPeople.name: Robert Schuman
keyPeople.text: Born in Luxembourg; a founding father of the European Union.
